slot.brief: Given a function f(x) (e.g., f(x) = x + 1/x style), check whether it is one-one/onto and find its inverse if it exists

stem: Let $f:[1,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be defined by $f(x)=(x-1)^2$. Which statement is correct?
options: $f$ is one-one but not onto, so it has no inverse.
$f$ is onto but not one-one, so it has no inverse.

verdicts.working: For x≥1, f is strictly increasing and has range [0,∞). Solving y=(x−1)² gives x=1+√y, so f is bijective with the inverse in (A).

working:
$f'(x)=2(x-1)\geq 0$ for $x\geq1$, and $f$ is strictly increasing on $[1,\infty)$.
$f([1,\infty))=[0,\infty)$, so $f$ is onto its codomain.
$y=(x-1)^2$, with $x\geq1$, gives $x=1+\sqrt{y}$.
Thus $f^{-1}(x)=1+\sqrt{x}$.

Independent check: For x≥1, f is strictly increasing and has range [0,∞). Solving y=(x−1)² gives x=1+√y, so f is bijective with the inverse in (A).
solution:
For $x\geq1$, $f$ is strictly increasing and its range is $[0,\infty)$, so it is one-one and onto.
$$y=(x-1)^2\implies x=1+\sqrt{y},\qquad f^{-1}(x)=1+\sqrt{x}.$$
